ground_truth.description: Removed item counterbalancing — without it, discussed vs non-discussed comparison confounds item difficulty with experimental manipulation

matched_finding.description: The design section claims that 'discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced,' implying that which of the eight critical details are discussed versus not discussed varies systematically across participants or pairs. However, the procedure section explicitly states that 'each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase.' If the discussion set is fixed and identical across all pairs, full counterbalancing is impossible. The discussed vs. non-discussed distinction would be entirely confounded with item identity—any observed accuracy difference could reflect item-specific properties (inherent memorability, salience, visual distinctiveness) rather than the effect of misinformation exposure. This undermines the central within-subjects comparison on which the entire study rests.
matched_finding.quote: Design: 'In the study, the memory conformity effect will be measured in a within-subjects design and discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced.' Procedure: 'In order to ensure sufficient discussion, each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase.'

More precisely, if a pair of participants disagreed with each other and gave d...
ground_truth.modified_snippet: In addition, while scoring the individual memory test accuracy on the discussed questions (items containing misleading information), we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation, as the collaborative recall procedure is designed to expose participants to their partner’s ...
ground_truth.description: Removed disputed/non-disputed classification — treats all discussed items as containing misinformation when some may not have; conflates delivered vs non-delivered misinformation

matched_finding.description: The analysis plan first specifies a nuanced rule: if a partner provides an answer consistent with what the participant saw (e.g., guessing correctly), that item is NOT classified as containing misinformation and should not be scored as a misleading trial. However, the very next paragraph contradicts this by stating 'we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation, as the collaborative recall procedure is designed to expose participants to their partner's differing version of events.' These two rules are mutually incompatible: the first is item-specific and condition-dependent; the second is categorical and ignores actual discussion content. Applying the categorical rule inflates the misinformation exposure count by including cases where no misinformation was actually introduced, attenuating the observed conformity effect and biasing analyses of its reduction.
matched_finding.quote: 'However, if the partner provided an answer consistent with what the participant had seen, that is, "white mug" (such a situation can happen, e.g., as a result of the partner's guessing), the situation will not be classified as misleading.' vs. 'we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation, as the collaborative recall procedure is designed to expose participants to their partner's differing version of events.'

The main reason for that is that we wanted to inoculate participants against the influence of misinformation before it could take eff...
ground_truth.description: Changed intervention from post- to pre-misinformation — tests encoding prevention instead of retrieval resistance; invalidates IMP theoretical framework which requires post-exposure placement

matched_finding.description: The introduction explicitly states that all three interventions will be placed BEFORE the collaborative recall phase, framing them as inoculation against incoming misinformation. The methods and procedure section, however, places the interventions AFTER the collaborative recall and a second filler task, immediately before the individual memory test. These two placements are not equivalent: pre-collaborative-recall placement could alter the social dynamics of the discussion itself (e.g., participants may challenge each other differently), whereas post-collaborative-recall placement functions solely as a post-warning before the memory test. The entire theoretical rationale built on IMP and informational influence is developed assuming participants have already been exposed to misinformation when the intervention acts. The contradiction makes it impossible to determine what study was actually designed and what theoretical claims are being tested.
matched_finding.quote: Introduction: 'What is important, we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation before the collaborative recall phase (that is, before exposing participants to misinformation).' Methods 2.5: 'The procedure will consist of four main phases: (1) presenting the original material, (2) collaborative recall (including misinformation), (3) three procedures to reduce vulnerability to misinformation (and a control condition), and (4) an individual memory test of the original material.'

ground_truth.original_snippet: we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect has little use in this study: participants work on their own and do not compare their answers with anybody, therefore there is little cost of disagreeing (although it is still possible that some pressure exists as the p...

ground_truth.description: Changed 'has little use' to 'completely ruled out' and removed experimenter-awareness caveat — overclaims mechanism specificity

matched_finding.description: The authors categorically exclude normative influence from consideration, arguing that because participants work individually without real-time comparison, there is 'no cost of disagreeing.' This conflates the absence of concurrent social presence with the absence of normative motivation. Internalized social norms from the prior discussion persist during private testing; participants may feel interpersonal obligation to the partner with whom they just conversed, anticipate post-study comparison of answers, or experience discomfort at the thought of contradicting someone face-to-face. Empirical research on private conformity (e.g., Deutsch & Gerard, 1955) establishes precisely that normative influence operates even absent direct observation. Dismissing this as 'completely ruled out' is theoretically unjustifiable and leads the authors to attribute all conformity effects to informational influence, which then restricts their predictions about which interventions should work and for whom—potentially producing incorrect hypotheses.
matched_finding.quote: Given the fact that the individual memory test does not include any element of direct interpersonal pressure, we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect is completely ruled out in this study: participants work on their own and do not compare their answers with anybody, therefore there is no cost of disagreeing.

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Open-ended→forced-choice changes baseline conformity rate and scoring categories — must know format matters
ground_truth.original_snippet: In the present research, the individual memory test will be in the form of open-ended questions.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: In the present research, the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format.
ground_truth.description: Changed from open-ended to forced-choice — inflates conformity rates (50% guessing baseline vs much lower); scoring categories (correct, misinformation, other) don't make sense with forced-choice

matched_finding.description: The procedure section describes the individual memory test as consisting of open-ended questions with four derived scoring indices (correct, misinformation-consistent, other, and total). The analysis plan section then describes using a two-alternative forced-choice format for the same test. These are fundamentally different response formats: open-ended responses can yield 'other' and 'don't know' answers, while forced-choice constrains responses to two options and cannot produce 'other' responses. The four-index scoring system explicitly mentioned for the ANOVA analysis is only possible with open-ended responses. Yet the analysis plan simultaneously describes the two-alternative forced-choice scoring logic used in prior MORI studies. This contradiction makes it impossible to determine the actual test format, the valid scoring procedure, or what prior effect sizes are relevant benchmarks.
matched_finding.quote: Procedure: 'The test will contain 20 open-ended questions, eight of which will cover all the critical details included in the movie.' Analysis plan: 'In the present research, the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format.'

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Co-witness exposure exclusion removed — must know non-exposed participants dilute the effect
ground_truth.original_snippet: In addition, participants who are not exposed to co-witness details at all (that is, the participants who did not hear any potentially misleading information from the partner) will be excluded from the analyses.
ground_truth.description: Removed exclusion of non-exposed participants — including those who received zero misinformation dilutes the conformity effect and biases against finding both the basic effect and intervention benefit
